🇲🇽📚 <u>UNAM OWNS ITS MISTAKE: ADMISSION EXAMS GO BACK IN PERSON</u>

After its digital admission test failed, Mexico’s UNAM is returning to in-person exams — and its rector didn’t dodge it: “The University and its rector take responsibility for the failures and the errors.” Tests will run on pre-loaded devices across multiple sites, with a new AI council to steer the technology. A public university held to account by its own students, not by spin.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON’S OWN FILES: TORTURE AND 26,121 DISAPPEARED UNDER CALDERÓN & PEÑA</u>

The same US that armed Calderón’s drug war quietly documented the results. A 2013 State Department human-rights report logged 7,000 unidentified bodies and 26,121 people disappeared between 2006 and 2012 — unlawful killings, torture and forced disappearances by Mexican security forces. This was the “partnership” era run by security chief Genaro García Luna, now convicted in a US court of taking Sinaloa Cartel bribes.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE MAN WHO BUILT FOBAPROA STILL COLLECTS 149,203 PESOS A MONTH</u>

AMLO cancelled the lifetime pensions of every living ex-president — Salinas, Fox, Calderón, Peña. But Ernesto Zedillo, architect of the Fobaproa bank bailout, still pockets 149,203 pesos a month (1.79 million a year), paid not by the Presidency but by the Banco de México. The rescue he once sold as costing “only 180 billion pesos” has cost Mexicans 1.6 trillion pesos in interest alone since 1997 — with zero principal paid.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO’S FALLEN STEEL GIANT DRAWS 6 BIDDERS AFTER YEARS OF SILENCE</u>

Altos Hornos de México — the Coahuila steel giant idle since March 2023 — now has six qualified bidders lined up for its September 25 auction, with a floor of 1,127 million dollars. The February attempt drew zero bids; Sheinbaum’s government pressed to sell AHMSA and Minosa as a single productive unit and reactivate the plant for the workers it left stranded. Monclova may get its furnaces back.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>MEXICO CAN NOW FIRE AN ELECTED JUDGE FOR CORRUPTION — AND JUST DID</u>

The opposition swore judicial elections would shield criminals. In Chihuahua, Manuel Jurado — voted onto the bench this June under AMLO’s judicial reform — became the first elected judge criminally prosecuted for corruption, forced to resign after illegally altering a precautionary measure to free a man being tried for rape and domestic violence. Accountability the old appointed judiciary never delivered.
banner: MEXICO OUSTS 1ST ELECTED JUDGE FOR GRAFT

text: 🇲🇽🛡️ The history of a people that never kneels before any foreign power. "That is the history of Mexico — the history of a people that never surrenders, that never kneels before any foreign power." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Honestidad y Resultados, Quintana Roo She traced Mexico's sovereignty from Morelos to Juárez: the Pastry War, the U.S. invasion that took half the territory, the French intervention — and how the conservatives, "like today, went to Europe" to bring Maximilian. Juárez never recognized them.

🇲🇽📈 They warned that raising wages would bring inflation. It rose 154% — and there was none. "The minimum wage rose by 154 percent... In 2018 it was 2,800 pesos; now it's more than 9,500 — and there was no inflation. The peso is one of the strongest currencies in the world, and we're at a record for foreign direct investment. This model works." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Honestidad y Resultados, Quintana Roo Neoliberal orthodoxy warned that higher wages meant inflation, devaluation, and capital flight. None of it happened.
📸 Honestidad y Resultados en Quintana Roo — Cancún, Quintana Roo · 12 de septiembre de 2026

🇲🇽🌊 2 billion pesos more to fight the sargassum. Sheinbaum announced an extra 2-billion-peso plan with the Navy — more boats and cleanup crews — after an unusually heavy sargassum year on Quintana Roo's coast. She also confirmed Tren Maya cargo service begins next year and pointed to the newly inaugurated Nichupté bridge in Cancún. — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Honestidad y Resultados, Quintana Roo

🇲🇽❤️ "For the good of all — first the poor." In Quintana Roo, 486,167 people now receive a welfare program: 116,690 seniors on the Universal Pension, 60,617 students with Benito Juárez scholarships, and 23,000 people with disabilities — a 9.24-billion-peso yearly investment that goes straight to families. — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Honestidad y Resultados, Quintana Roo
